channel.title: Daily Teams News summaries
channel.description: Plain-English daily summaries of Microsoft Teams documentation and Message Center changes.

item.title: Passwordless sign-in guidance adds Authenticator and Conditional Access prerequisites for personal Teams phones — 13 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 13 November 2026

Passwordless sign-in guidance adds Authenticator and Conditional Access prerequisites for personal Teams phones

The period’s clearest administrator-facing addition is new guidance for passwordless sign-in on personally assigned Teams phones without device code flow. It specifies prerequisites, registration, and Conditional Access setup, while noting that the option does not satisfy phishing-resistant authentication requirements. Other meaningful updates clarify network, Intelligent Recap retention, and shared-mailbox recording behavior; much of the remaining activity repairs Teams Phone agent links.

Devices · General

New passwordless sign-in guidance for personal Teams phones

The new guidance explains how to use Microsoft Authenticator passwordless phone sign-in for personally assigned Teams phones without device code flow. It covers prerequisites, registration, and Conditional Access configuration, but the option does not meet phishing-resistant authentication requirements.

Clients · General

Network guidance specifies relay DNS and UDP 49152–53247

The guidance now explains DNS-based relay discovery and warns that blocked relay-name resolution can prevent calls or media. It also identifies UDP 49152–53247 for Direct Routing non-media-bypass calls, giving administrators concrete DNS, proxy, and firewall checks.

Meetings and events · AI and Copilot

Intelligent Recap retention uses an explicit day range

The setting is documented under **Copilot and other AI** as **Set a default expiration time for Intelligent Recap .docx files for non-transcribed meetings**. Administrators can set retention from 1 to 9999 days, or use -1 for no expiration.

Meetings and events · General

Unlicensed shared mailboxes follow the global meeting policy for recording

The updated guidance states that shared mailboxes without a Teams license use the global identity’s meeting policy. When global cloud recording is disabled, users cannot record meetings organized by those mailboxes.

Teams Phone · AI and Copilot

Teams Phone agent links now target configurable call-length guidance

The cmdlet setup article’s references for configurable maximum call length and maximum call length now point to the “What’s new: configurable call length” section. The settings remain documented as configurable in Teams admin center.

View all updates for 13 November 2026 →

item.title: Facilitator will resolve meeting knowledge gaps with web answers starting February — 12 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 12 November 2026

Facilitator will resolve meeting knowledge gaps with web answers starting February

Teams is preparing Facilitator for availability from February 2027. It will detect meeting knowledge gaps and provide web-search answers in chat, subject to Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), manual enablement, and admin and user controls. Event recording access is also shifting to event-specific settings, while channel meetings gain broader scheduling and discovery capabilities. Other updates provide operational guidance for Direct Routing and passwordless Teams Android deployments.

Teams · AI and Copilot

Facilitator adds web-search answers to meeting chat

Facilitator will detect and resolve knowledge gaps by providing relevant answers through web search in meeting chat. It becomes available from February 2027, requires Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), must be manually enabled, and supports admin controls and user opt-out.

Teams · Policies and settings

Event recording access shifts to town hall and webinar settings

For Events App town halls and webinars, the "Who has access to the recording or transcript" option will follow RecordingForTownhall or RecordingForWebinar rather than AllowCloudRecording. Worldwide rollout is scheduled for early to mid-November 2026, with no admin action required.

Teams · General

Channel meetings add Outlook, calendar, and delegate scheduling

The enhanced channel meeting experience will support scheduling from the Teams calendar and Outlook, improve discovery for channel members, and add delegate scheduling. Rollout starts in November 2026 and completes by September 2027 across environments; Microsoft recommends informing users but requires no admin action.

Teams Phone · General

Direct Routing guidance defines SBC health through SIP OPTIONS

Updated protocol guidance explains TLS validation, tenant lookup, and bidirectional SIP OPTIONS exchanges, with successful responses marking an SBC Active. It clarifies that SBC health reflects SIP OPTIONS rather than call traffic, and that hosted derived SBCs use the status of the main physical SBC. These distinctions support troubleshooting of Inactive states and SIP OPTIONS warnings.

Teams Rooms · General

Passwordless Teams Android guidance covers Device Code Flow refreshes

The updated passwordless resource-account guidance states that Teams Android devices signed in with Device Code Flow continue using DCF when authentication tokens refresh. It also calls out considerations for organizations that block DCF with Conditional Access.

View all updates for 12 November 2026 →

item.title: PMP requires Admin Agent 901 update as TAC device management deprecation approaches — 11 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 11 November 2026

PMP requires Admin Agent 901 update as TAC device management deprecation approaches

Most of the 18 entries are documentation maintenance, but several carry direct operational weight. Admin Agent 901 adds Android 15 connectivity and provisioning fixes, cannot be paused, and is required for PMP device management. Teams Phone guidance documents authorized-user active-call controls and updated recording disclosures, while VDI HID guidance tightens version and architecture prerequisites. Teams Rooms guidance also sets a January 2027 retirement for M365 Targeted Release.

Devices · General

Admin Agent 901 adds Android 15 fixes and is required for PMP management

Certified Device Apps identifies version 1.0.0.202610190119 (Admin Agent 901) as adding critical Android 15 connectivity and provisioning fixes. The release is being accelerated across all Teams-certified devices, cannot be paused, is required to manage devices in PMP, and prepares for TAC device-management deprecation targeted for mid-November 2026.

Teams Phone · PowerShell and automation

Call-queue guidance documents four authorized-user active-call controls

The Teams Phone call-queue cmdlet guidance states, effective November 10, 2026, that authorized users can join active calls through Monitor, Whisper, Barge, and Takeover.

Teams Phone · AI and Copilot

Teams Phone Agent greeting explains recording and transcription handling

The setup guidance changes the greeting to tell callers that calls are recorded. It states that calls are recorded and transcribed for service quality, inaccessible to humans, and deleted after processing; configured automatic recording greetings are used instead.

Clients · General

VDI HID guidance sets Teams version and client architecture prerequisites

HID now requires Teams 26276.x.x.x or later. Citrix Workspace supports x86 or x64 MSIX packages, while Windows App and Horizon clients are 64-bit only; the previous HID Public Preview note was removed.

Teams Rooms · General

Teams Rooms guidance sets January 2027 retirement for M365 Targeted Release

The Mtr Home Refresh page now references Microsoft Frontier and states that M365 Targeted Release is retiring in January 2027.

View all updates for 11 November 2026 →

item.title: Teams Free off-network invitations retire as OneDrive video sharing reaches Teams events — 10 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 10 November 2026

Teams Free off-network invitations retire as OneDrive video sharing reaches Teams events

The period brings a December 2026 retirement for off-network invitations to Teams Free, alongside mid-November rollouts for direct OneDrive video sharing in Teams events and policy-aligned recording controls. Teams also adds malicious QR-code detection through existing Malicious URL protection. The remaining updates are mainly Teams Rooms reference and hardware documentation changes.

Teams · General

Off-network invitations to Teams Free will be retired

Starting in December 2026, users will no longer be able to invite external people by email or chat links to create Teams Free accounts. Existing Teams Free collaboration and federation remain unchanged, but user-facing guidance should be updated.

Teams · General

Teams events will support direct OneDrive video sharing

Beginning in mid-November 2026, event organizers and producers can share OneDrive videos through “Manage what attendees see,” enabling playback without screen sharing or embedding the video in PowerPoint. No administrator action is required.

Teams · Policies and settings

Meeting recording controls will reflect assigned policies

From mid-November through mid-December 2026, meeting options will show automatic recording and transcription choices allowed by the organizer’s assigned policies, including a new “Record only” option.

Teams · General

Teams will detect malicious QR codes in chats and channels

Starting in mid-November 2026, Teams will warn about harmful QR-code links, with external QR codes blurred by default. The capability is enabled through existing Malicious URL protection and requires no separate administrator action.

Teams Rooms · General

Teams Rooms references add PTZ support and a certified room kit

The Teams Devices Feature Comparison now marks local pan-tilt-zoom controls as available in three rows, while the certified hardware list adds the AVer CORE500 Room Kit with a Core Ultra 5 processor, 16 GB of memory, and 256 GB of storage. These updates support device evaluation rather than signaling a new Teams Rooms rollout.

View all updates for 10 November 2026 →

item.title: Teams guidance shifts from webinar and town hall names to audience-based event labels — 7 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 7 November 2026

Teams guidance shifts from webinar and town hall names to audience-based event labels

The period is dominated by terminology and procedure updates rather than product rollouts. Updated event guidance now uses “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience” across recording, attendance, setup, captions, publishing, and chat topics. A separate Teams Rooms update revises screenshots and the note-saving workflow.

Teams · Policies and settings

Policy references adopt audience-based event labels

The Settings Policies Reference now uses “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience” instead of webinar and town hall terminology across related settings. Use the revised labels when locating policy controls.

Meetings and events · General

Recording guidance documents separate audience-size event settings

The Meeting Recording article now groups webinars and town halls under events and documents settings for events with up to 1,000 attendees or for large audiences. It also clarifies policy-assignment instructions.

Meetings and events · General

Anonymous-attendance instructions use the new event names

The guide replaces “Who can attend webinars” and “Who can attend town halls” with “Who can attend events up to 1k attendees” and “Who can attend events optimized for a large audience,” and updates the configuration steps for anonymous participants.

Meetings and events · General

Event registration setting receives a new documented name

The setting formerly documented as “Webinar registration form questions” is now called “Events registration form questions.” Administrators should update internal configuration references and runbooks that use the previous name.

Teams Rooms · AI and Copilot

Teams Rooms note-saving workflow and visuals are revised

The Facilitator Teams Rooms article updates screenshots, preview wording, and instructions for adding participant names when saving notes so participants can access notes and transcripts later. The revised workflow is useful for user guidance, with no administrator configuration change stated.

View all updates for 7 November 2026 →

item.title: Teams Rooms app update tool is no longer recommended for new Autopilot deployments — 6 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 6 November 2026

Teams Rooms app update tool is no longer recommended for new Autopilot deployments

This was a quiet, documentation-led day with one actionable Teams Rooms change. The Autopilot guidance says the Teams Rooms app has included automatic updates since April 2024, so the app update tool is no longer recommended for new deployments. A separate known-issues entry records possible Large Gallery unavailability on specified Teams Rooms for Android versions, while release notes document a low-bitrate video fix. Teams Phone updates only reorder language entries in reference and setup material.

Teams Rooms · General

Autopilot guidance changes the app update tool recommendation

Because the Teams Rooms app has included automatic updates since April 2024, the app update tool is no longer recommended for new deployments. Administrators should review Intune configurations and consider unassigning the tool, except when deploying devices older than 2025.

Devices · Troubleshooting

Large Gallery may be unavailable on specified Teams Rooms for Android versions

The known-issues page identifies possible Large Gallery unavailability on Teams Rooms for Android app versions 1449/1.0.96.2026249711 through 1449/1.0.96.2026264504. The issue is expected to be addressed in a future update, and no administrator action is specified.

Teams Rooms · General

Release notes record a low-bitrate video fix

Teams Rooms release notes now document a fix for certain devices sending low-bitrate video in specific meeting scenarios. The supplied evidence states no administrator action.

View all updates for 6 November 2026 →

item.title: Teams will organize muted and meeting chats into dedicated sections in January — 5 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 5 November 2026

Teams will organize muted and meeting chats into dedicated sections in January

Microsoft Teams will introduce a January 2027 chat reorganization: the Muted chats section will be enabled by default, while Meeting chats will be disabled by default, with users able to toggle and reorder both. Two worldwide changes are also planned for December 2026: a Workflows template that links team tags to channel membership and mobile call declines with chat messages. Documentation updates add certified-device entries and SlimCore troubleshooting detail.

Teams · General

Muted and meeting chats get dedicated sections in January 2027

Teams will add Muted chats and Meeting chats sections. Muted chats will be enabled by default, while Meeting chats will be disabled by default. Users can enable or disable and reorder the sections, and muted chats move automatically unless they are favorited. Rollout begins in January 2027, with no admin action required.

Teams · General

Workflows will connect team tags to channel membership

An optional Workflows app template will automatically add users to channels when they are added to a team tag. The feature rolls out worldwide in mid-December 2026 and does not change defaults.

Teams · General

Teams mobile users will be able to decline calls with messages

Users will be able to decline incoming Teams mobile calls with a predefined or custom message sent through Teams chat. Worldwide rollout is scheduled for December 2026; the feature applies only to Teams-to-Teams calls with available chat and requires no admin action.

Devices · General

Certified Hardware Android adds Meeting Owl and Cisco entries

The table now includes Meeting Owl 5 Pro, Owl Tablet, and multiple Cisco devices, along with their associated software versions and certification dates. Administrators can use these details when validating inventories and planning deployments.

Clients · Troubleshooting

SlimCore troubleshooting adds Windows error 6/51 guidance

Vdi 2 Troubleshooting now documents Windows error 6/51, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE, during SlimCore download, deployment, or startup, and points administrators to BITS Client and AppXDeployment-Server logs.

View all updates for 5 November 2026 →
